summary: Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Kalu Rinpoche in 1973.

Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (~1853–1870), Thegchog Dorje, Gyurme Thutop Namgyal, and the 9th Tai Situpa Pema Nyingche Wangpo.

Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. As of 2016, he held professorships at Smith College.

Jampa Losang Panglung specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery (-1958) and completed a Magister and Promotion at the University of Munich (~1969–1979). He worked at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1974–2005).
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Stewart studied under traditional teachers Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge and Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (attested 1995).

Jampa Samten is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as Director (attested 1991) and later Professor (attested 2015) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jamsrangiin Tseveen was a scholar of linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1905), headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences (~1921–1932), and worked at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1932–1937).

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsab, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga, and succeeded Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye (~1840–1892), Minling Trichen Gyurme Sangye Kunga, Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, and numerous other traditional teachers.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Jan C. Heesterman was an Indologist. He held an appointment at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990, serving as Professor.

Jan Chozen Bays works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from Swarthmore College (~1962–1966) and UC San Diego (~1968–1972), studied under Taizan Maezumi (1977–1995) and Shodo Harada (1990), and became abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery (~2002).
Jan Dolensky is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Dolensky studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes at the University of Vienna, earning a Magister der Philosophie (attested 2013).

Jan Fontein worked in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Leiden University (PhD under Theodoor Paul Galestin) and held curatorial posts at the Rijksmuseum (1947–1955+) and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Utrecht University (1923–1929) and studied at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and the Indology chair (1932–1976) at Utrecht University, succeeding Johannes Rahder.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1873–1877) and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).
Jan Jaworski was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1923–1930) and under Stanisław Schayer (~1925–1930) and Jean Przyluski (~1930–1932).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University (Promotion 1908–1928), Sorbonne University, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as Dozent (1919) and Professor of Chinese Language and Literature (1930–1954) at Leiden University.

Jan N. Bremmer is a scholar of religious studies and history. He earned his PhD from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam. He was Assistant Professor at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and Chair of Religious Studies at Groningen (1990–2009).

Jan Nattier is a Buddhist and Central Asian studies scholar. She completed graduate work at Indiana University and a PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. She held professorships at Indiana University (1992–2005) and Soka University / IRIAB (2004–2013).
